name: Meteorite
toxicityNote: Iron meteorite can rust and stain skin or surfaces; keep dry and wash hands if pieces are rusty.
emotional: Eases feeling small in a big world
physical: Crystal healers link it to a feeling of solidity
Many people carry it for stamina during demanding days
summary: Meteorite meaning and lore: pieces of space rock that carry the patterns of the cosmos, prized for grounding, perspective and spiritual connection.
intro: A meteorite is a piece of asteroid, planet or moon that survived the fiery fall through Earth's atmosphere and landed intact. Iron meteorites, the type most often sold in crystal shops, are dense, heavy and rust-brown or silver-grey on the outside. When a slice is polished and lightly etched with acid, it reveals the Widmanstatten pattern: a crosshatch of interlocking metal crystals that can only form when molten metal cools over millions of years inside a space body. Stony meteorites, such as chondrites, look like dark rocks with tiny glittering metal flakes and sometimes a black, melted crust. Holding one feels strangely heavy for its size.
history: Humans have prized meteorites for millennia. Ancient Egyptians called iron the metal from heaven, and beads of meteoritic iron have been found in predynastic tombs. Tutankhamun was buried with a dagger whose blade is now known to be made of meteoritic iron. Many cultures worshipped fallen stones; the Black Stone at the Kaaba in Mecca and a stone venerated at Ephesus are famous examples. In the Arctic, Inuit people made tools from iron fragments of the Cape York meteorite for centuries. Modern collecting has grown into a global trade, with strewn fields in Namibia, Sweden, Argentina, Morocco and Siberia, and meteorites are now studied as time capsules of the early solar system.
meaning: Meteorite is cherished as a stone of cosmic perspective, strength and ancient memory. Practitioners say it links the Root with the Crown and Soul Star, joining earth and sky, and that holding it can give a sense of being part of something vast. It is linked with resilience, since it survived heat and impact, and many people use it to find steady footing during upheaval. Some feel it encourages bold thinking and a willingness to explore new paths. In ritual, it is often kept on an altar as a symbol of origins and as a gentle protector. It is also associated with deep meditation, as its metallic weight is thought to anchor visions to the body. These beliefs are traditional associations, not medical statements.
howToUse: Hold a small piece during meditation and picture the long journey it made through space before reaching you. Keep a pendant or pocket piece close when you need strength and resilience. Place a slice on an altar or shelf as a focus for reflection, ideally beside a clear quartz point. When stargazing, hold it as you look up. In a grid, use it at the centre for cosmic energy or at the base for grounding. Always keep iron meteorite dry and wear it only if sealed or lacquered.
care: Iron meteorite rusts easily, so keep it dry and never soak it. Wipe gently with a soft dry cloth, and add a thin film of mineral oil or microcrystalline wax to protect it. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or by resting it on a selenite plate. Sunlight is safe but unnecessary. Store in a dry box with a silica gel packet. Keep stony meteorites away from damp too, since the metal flakes can oxidise. Wash your hands after handling rusty pieces, and do not make elixirs.
identify: Iron meteorites are heavy, magnetic and show the Widmanstatten pattern when etched. Stony meteorites often have a thin, dark fusion crust and tiny metal flakes inside, also attracted to a magnet. Beware of slag, hematite, magnetite and iron-rich terrestrial rocks sold as meteorites; they often lack the crystal pattern or fusion crust. Fakes also include cast metal with etched patterns. Buy pieces with authentication from a reputable dealer and a stated source such as Gibeon or Campo del Cielo.

faq.q: What is a meteorite used for in crystal healing?
faq.a: In crystal tradition a meteorite is used for grounding, cosmic perspective and resilience. People keep it on altars, hold it in meditation or wear it as a pendant to feel connected to the wider universe.

faq.q: How can I tell if a rock is a meteorite?
faq.a: Check for heavy weight, magnetism, a thin black fusion crust and tiny metal flakes inside. Iron meteorites show a crosshatch pattern when etched. For certainty, ask a reputable dealer or lab, since many earth rocks mimic meteorites.

faq.q: Can I get a meteorite wet?
faq.a: It is best to keep iron meteorites dry, since water causes rust. Wipe them with a soft cloth, apply a light protective wax or oil, and cleanse them with smoke, sound or moonlight instead of water.
